Key facts:
- Same-sex conduct lawful since 2015 penal code; no criminalisation of gender identity. So no criminal exposure on that basis.
- No legal gender recognition procedure — resident-facing, climate signal only.
- Penal code Articles 191 (incitement to discrimination/hatred/violence based on gender identity) and 160 (gender identity as aggravating factor in homicide). No recorded prosecution — paper protections not shown to operate.
- No anti-discrimination protections in education, health, housing, employment; employment protection repealed 2023/2024.
- Advertising code covers sexual orientation, not necessarily gender identity.
- Highest court 2017 struck down moral order clause, allowed only LGBT org to register. Civil society functioning.
- Societal attitudes broadly neutral; family ostracisation, employment/education barriers for residents.
- 2015 activist statement: not targeted by violence as elsewhere, but discrimination real.
- No trans-specific violence data. No info on prison housing, entry screening, document marker treatment, care access.
- Traveller-facing: nothing documented on border/document treatment of trans travellers — uncertain, no evidence of targeting. No bathroom/facility ban documented. No police profiling documented (general police detentions noted, no trans-specific).
- No criminalisation. No documented state threat-framing against trans visitors.
- Social friction level: broadly neutral attitudes, dated surveys.

So the worst documented feature: societal discrimination for residents, absence of anti-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition. None of these are traveller-facing exposures per rubric. No documented universal-exposure measures, no organised targeting, no criminal statute. Paper protection (Art 191/160) present but not shown to operate — tier 5.

So this is a "no criminalisation, broadly neutral society, thin formal recourse for residents, paper protections unverified, no documented trans-specific violence, open questions about documents/prison/care" — per rule 13, that sits a step below the acceptance-with-protections tier. Comparable to 0.65 anchors: countries with law protecting but inconsistent practice/remedies working. Here remedies not documented working (no prosecutions under Art 191), employment protection repealed, but no active traveller restriction.

Hmm. Compare to 0.65-A/B/C/D/E: those have documented protections working effectively (courts overturning, ombudsperson intervening) with some friction. Here we have no documented traveller-facing protection operating, no documented incident. Paper protections (Art 191) exist but unproven.

Rule 3 burden-of-proof symmetry: documented positives count; here documented positive is law prohibiting incitement on gender identity and aggravating factor — paper. Documented negative: repeal of employment protection (resident), absence of recognition (resident). Absence of trans-specific violence is in a moderately documented state (it has international org reporting, UN involvement, LGBT org) — so silence there is a moderately positive signal? The dossier explicitly says no trans-specific violence figure appears; activist 2015 statement says not targeted by violence. That's a dated positive.

No documented traveller-specific exposure at all. Rate the consequences if outed: no criminal penalty, society broadly neutral, but no effective anti-discrimination recourse; potential discrimination in services, family ostracisation (not applicable for visitor), no facility bans documented, no prison info.

I'd place this around 0.60-0.65. Given the absence of any documented traveller-facing harm and neutral society, but with unverified protections and no positive documented functioning remedies for visitors, plus dated data — I'd say ~0.62. Slightly below the 0.65 anchors because those anchors document remedies actually working for the visitor (apology, compensation, ombudsperson reversal), whereas here remedies are paper only and the employment protection was recently rolled back (climate signal slightly negative, though resident-facing).

Also the 2017 survey with 28% saying they'd assault their child if gay — that's dated, sexual-orientation framed, general population hostility signal. It's not trans-specific but signals social hostility exists in a segment. Still, 85% opposed violence.

Let's settle at 0.62.

Here nothing trans-specific traveller-facing documented. Survey prevalence is dated and LGB-wide. So Reduced Risk band (0.60-0.80) fits. 0.62 is at the bottom edge of Reduced Risk. Reasonable.

Good.
